answer: In an AI agent economy, sybil resistance can rely on a stake-weighted attestation graph. Each agent posts a bond that acts as a beacon of commitment; peers only route high-value tasks through agents whose bonds remain locked at a shared jetty of collateral. When an attacker spins up many cheap identities, the required aggregate stake grows linearly while the expected payoff from diluting a river of rewards stays sub-linear, so the attack becomes unprofitable. Honest agents further raise the cost by requiring multi-hop vouching that burns stake on false positives.
